sn22.15:1.5: This directly rejects all forms of self, but especially the Upaniṣadic view. For Pali _eso’hamasmi_, see _so’hamasmi_ (“I am that”) at Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.4.1, which parallels the echoes Uddālaka’s famous description of the “subtlest’ self: “all that is the truth, that is the self, you are that” (_sarvaṁ tatsatyaṁ sa ātmā tattvamasi_, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7, etc.). In particular the phrase _tattvamasi_ is an exact parallel (in second person) to the Pali _esohamasmi_. See too Uddālaka’s, “I am that, I indeed am that” (_iyam aham asmīyam aham asmīti_, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.10.1; cf. 4.11.1, 4.12.1, 8.11.1–2). Likewise it is said, “I myself am that person” (_yo’sāvasau puruṣaḥ so’hamasmi_, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 5.15 = Īśā Upaniṣad 16). Depending on context, similar phrases might also depict the one who is attached to a false, limited self, thinking “I am he”, “this is mine” (_ahaṁ so, mamedaṁ_, Maitrī Upaniṣad 3.2). His first words _ahamasmi brahmā_ (“I am Brahmā”) are equivalent to _aham brahmāsmīti_ at 1.4.10.  at [mn28:6.8]() etc.
